Walking Dead (season 7)">Season 7</A></DIV>\n<DIV style="float: right;"></DIV>\n</TD>\n</TR>\n<TR>\n<TD colspan="2" class="noprint" style="text-align:center"><A href="/wiki/List_of_The_Walking_Dead_episodes" title="List of The Walking Dead episodes">List of <I>The Walking Dead</I> episodes</A></TD>\n</TR>\n</TBODY></TABLE>\n<P>The eighth season of <I><A href="/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_(TV_series)" title="The Walking Dead (TV series)">The Walking Dead</A></I>, an American <A href="/wiki/Apocalyptic_and_post-apocalyptic_fiction" title="Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic fiction">post-apocalyptic</A> <A href="/wiki/Horror_fiction" title="Horror fiction">horror</A> <A href="/wiki/Television_series" class="mw-redirect" title="Television series">television series</A> on <A href="/wiki/AMC_(TV_channel)" title="AMC (TV channel)">AMC</A>, premiered on October 22, 2017,<SUP id="cite_ref-S8premiere_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-S8premiere-1">[1]</A></SUP> and will consist of 16 episodes<SUP id="cite_ref-ew_s8_2-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ew_s8-2">[2]</A></SUP> split into two eight-episode parts, with the second part debuting on February 25, 2018.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>Developed for television by <A href="/wiki/Frank_Darabont" title="Frank Darabont">Frank Darabont</A>, the series is based on the <A href="/wiki/The_Walking_Dead_(comic_book)" title="The Walking Dead (comic book)">eponymous series of comic books</A> by <A href="/wiki/Robert_Kirkman" title="Robert Kirkman">Robert Kirkman</A>, <A href="/wiki/Tony_Moore_(artist)" title="Tony Moore (artist)">Tony Moore</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Charlie_Adlard" title="Charlie Adlard">Charlie Adlard</A>. The executive producers are Kirkman, David Alpert, <A href="/wiki/Scott_M._Gimple" title="Scott M. Gimple">Scott M. Gimple</A>, <A href="/wiki/Greg_Nicotero" title="Greg Nicotero">Greg Nicotero</A>, <A href="/wiki/Tom_Luse" title="Tom Luse">Tom Luse</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Gale_Anne_Hurd" title="Gale Anne Hurd">Gale Anne Hurd</A>, with Gimple as <A href="/wiki/Showrunner" title="Showrunner">showrunner</A> for the fifth consecutive season. The eighth season has received mostly positive reviews.</P>\n<P>This season adapts the &quot;All Out War&quot; story arc from the comics, with the survivors of the Alexandria Safe-Zone, the Hilltop, the Kingdom, and later the Scavengers taking on <A href="/wiki/Negan" title="Negan">Negan</A> (<A href="/wiki/Jeffrey_Dean_Morgan" title="Jeffrey Dean Morgan">Jeffrey Dean Morgan</A>) and the Saviors.<SUP id="cite_ref-s8regulars_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-s8regulars-4">[4]</A></SUP></P>\n<P></P>\n<DIV id="toc" class="toc">\n<DIV class="toctitle" lang="en" dir="ltr" href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=13" title="Edit section: Production">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<P><I>The Walking Dead</I> was renewed by AMC for a 16-episode eighth season on October 16, 2016,<SUP id="cite_ref-ew_s8_2-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-ew_s8-2">[2]</A></SUP> and that same month it was reported that <A href="/wiki/Maria_Bello" title="Maria Bello">Maria Bello</A> would have a role on the show.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> Production began on April 25, 2017, in <A href="/wiki/Atlanta,_Georgia" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlanta, Georgia">Atlanta, Georgia</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> On July 12, 2017, production was shut down after stuntman <A href="/wiki/John_Bernecker" title="John Bernecker">John Bernecker</A> was killed, after falling more than 20 feet onto a concrete floor.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> Production resumed on July 17.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>The season premiere, which also serves as the series&#39; milestone <A href="/wiki/100_episodes" title="100 episodes">100th episode</A>, was directed by executive producer <A href="/wiki/Greg_Nicotero" title="Greg Nicotero">Greg Nicotero</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Director801_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Director801-10">[10]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>In November 2017, it was announced that <A href="/wiki/Lennie_James" title="Lennie James">Lennie James</A> who portrays <A href="/wiki/Morgan_Jones_(The_Walking_Dead)" title="Morgan Jones (The Walking Dead)">Morgan Jones</A>, would be leaving <I>The Walking Dead</I> after the conclusion of this season, and he will join the cast of the spin-off series <I><A href="/wiki/Fear_the_Walking_Dead" title="Fear the Walking Dead">Fear the Walking Dead</A></I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Episodes">Episodes</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A Gregory attempts to have the Hilltop residents side with Negan, but they all firmly stand behind Maggie. trailer for the season was released on July 21, 2017, at <A href="/wiki/San_Diego_Comic-Con" title="San Diego Comic-Con">San Diego Comic-Con</A>. The second trailer was released on February 1, 2018, for the second part of the season.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Reception">Reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=16" title="Edit section: Reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Critical_response">Critical response</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=The_Walking_Dead_(season_8)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=17" title="Edit section: Critical response">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>\n<P>The eighth season of <I>The Walking Dead</I> has received mostly positive reviews from critics. On <A href="/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes" title="Rotten Tomatoes">Rotten Tomatoes</A>, the season holds a score of 73% with an <A href="/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean" title="Weighted arithmetic mean">average rating</A> of 6.9 out of 10, based on 13 reviews, and an average episode score of 69%. The site&#39;s critical consensus reads: &quot;<I>The Walking Dead</I><SPAN class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">&#39;</SPAN>s eighth season energizes its characters with some much-needed angst and action, though it&#39;s still occasionally choppy and lacking forward-moving plot progression.&quot;<SUP id="cite_ref-RT_S8_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-RT_S8-23">[23]</A></SUP></P>\n<CENTER>\n<TABLE class="wikitable" style="text-align:center; margin: 0 15px;">\n<CAPTION><I>The Walking Dead</I> (season 8): Critical reception by title="Portal:Hellenismos">Hellenismos portal</A></TD></TR><TR><TD style="text-align:right;font-size:115%;padding-top: 0.6em;"><DIV class="plainlinks hlist navbar mini"><UL><LI class="nv-view"><A href="/wiki/Template:Ancient_Greek_religion" title="Template:Ancient Greek religion"><ABBR title="View this template">v</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-talk"><A href="/wiki/Template_talk:Ancient_Greek_religion" title="Template talk:Ancient Greek religion"><ABBR title="Discuss this template">t</ABBR></A></LI><LI class="nv-edit"><A class="external text" href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Template:Ancient_Greek_religion&amp;action=edit"><ABBR title="Edit this template">e</ABBR></A></LI></UL></DIV></TD></TR></TBODY></TABLE>\n<P>In <A href="/wiki/Greek_mythology" title="Greek mythology">Greek mythology</A>, <B>Persephone</B> (<SPAN class="nowrap"><SPAN class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt"><A href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<SPAN style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><SPAN title="&#39;p&#39; in &#39;pie&#39;">p</SPAN><SPAN title="/ər/: &#39;er&#39; in &#39;letter&#39;">ər</SPAN><SPAN title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</SPAN><SPAN title="&#39;s&#39; in &#39;sigh&#39;">s</SPAN><SPAN title="/ɛ/: &#39;e&#39; in &#39;dress&#39;">ɛ</SPAN><SPAN title="&#39;f&#39; in &#39;find&#39;">f</SPAN><SPAN title="/ə/: &#39;a&#39; in &#39;about&#39;">ə</SPAN><SPAN title="&#39;n&#39; in &#39;nigh&#39;">n</SPAN><SPAN title="/i/: &#39;y&#39; in &#39;happy&#39;">i</SPAN></SPAN>/</A></SPAN></SPAN>; <A href="/wiki/Greek_language" title="Greek language">Greek</A>: <SPAN lang="el">Περσεφόνη</SPAN>), also called <B>Kore</B> (<SPAN class="nowrap"><SPAN class="IPA nopopups noexcerpt"><A href="/wiki/Help:IPA/English" title="Help:IPA/English">/<SPAN style="border-bottom:1px dotted"><SPAN title="/ˈ/: primary stress follows">ˈ</SPAN><SPAN title="&#39;k&#39; in &#39;kind&#39;">k</SPAN><SPAN title="/ɔːr/: &#39;ar&#39; in &#39;war&#39;">ɔːr</SPAN><SPAN title="/iː/: &#39;ee&#39; in &#39;fleece&#39;">iː</SPAN></SPAN>/</A></SPAN></SPAN>; &quot;the maiden&quot;), is the daughter of <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A> and <A href="/wiki/Demeter" title="Demeter">Demeter</A> and is the queen of the <A href="/wiki/Greek_underworld" title="Greek underworld">underworld</A>. <A href="/wiki/Homer" title="Homer">Homer</A> describes her as the formidable, venerable majestic princess of the underworld, who carries into effect the curses of men upon the souls of the dead. Persephone was married to <A href="/wiki/Hades" title="Hades">Hades</A>, the god of the underworld.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson462_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson462-1">[1]</A></SUP> The myth of her abduction represents her function as the <A href="/wiki/Personification" class="mw-redirect" title="Personification">personification</A> of <A href="/wiki/Vegetation" title="Vegetation">vegetation</A>, which shoots forth in <A href="/wiki/Spring_(season)" title="Spring (season)">spring</A> and withdraws into the earth after harvest; hence, she is also associated with spring as well as the fertility of vegetation. Similar myths appear in the <A href="/wiki/Orient" title="Orient">Orient</A>, in the cults of male gods like <A href="/wiki/Attis" title="Attis">Attis</A>, <A href="/wiki/Adonis" title="Adonis">Adonis</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Osiris" title="Osiris">Osiris</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> and in <A href="/wiki/Minoan_civilization" title="Minoan civilization">Minoan</A> <A href="/wiki/Crete" title="Crete">Crete</A>.\n</P><P>Persephone as a <A href="/wiki/Vegetation_deity" title="Vegetation deity">vegetation goddess</A> and her mother Demeter were the central figures of the <A href="/wiki/Eleusinian_mysteries" class="mw-redirect" title="Eleusinian mysteries">Eleusinian mysteries</A>, which promised the initiated a more enjoyable prospect after death. In some versions, Persephone is the mother of <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A>&#39;s sons <A href="/wiki/Dionysus" title="Dionysus">Dionysus</A>, <A href="/wiki/Iacchus" title="Iacchus">Iacchus</A>, or <A href="/wiki/Zagreus" title="Zagreus">Zagreus</A>. The origins of her cult are uncertain, but it was based on very old agrarian cults of agricultural communities.\n</P><P>Persephone was commonly worshipped along with Demeter and with the same mysteries. To her alone were dedicated the mysteries celebrated at Athens in the month of <A href="/wiki/Anthesterion" class="mw-redirect" title="Anthesterion">Anthesterion</A>. In <A href="/wiki/Art_in_ancient_Greece" class="mw-redirect" title="Art in ancient Greece">Classical Greek art</A>, Persephone is invariably portrayed robed, often carrying a <A href="https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/sheaf" class="extiw" title="wikt:sheaf">sheaf</A> of grain. She may appear as a mystical divinity with a sceptre and a little box, but she was mostly represented in the process of being carried off by <A href="/wiki/Hades_(mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Hades (mythology)">Hades</A>.\n</P><P>In <A href="/wiki/Roman_mythology" title="Roman mythology">Roman mythology</A>, she is called <A href="/wiki/Proserpina" title="Proserpina">Proserpina</A>, and her mother, <A href="/wiki/Ceres_(Roman_mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ceres (Roman mythology)">Ceres</A> and her father <A href="/wiki/Jupiter(Mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Jupiter(Mythology)">Jupiter</A>.\n</P>\n<DIV id="toc" class="toc"><INPUT type="checkbox" role="button" id="toctogglecheckbox" class="toctogglecheckbox" style="display:none" /><DIV
