title="Panticapaeum">Panticapaeum</A>, <A href="/wiki/Taurica" class="mw-redirect" title="Taurica">Taurica</A> (<A href="/wiki/Crimea" title="Crimea">Crimea</A>), <A href="/wiki/Bosporan_Kingdom" title="Bosporan Kingdom">Bosporan Kingdom</A></DIV></DIV></DIV>\n<P>Local cults of Demeter and Kore existed in Greece, <A href="/wiki/Asia_Minor" class="mw-redirect" title="Asia Minor">Asia Minor</A>, <A href="/wiki/Sicily" title="Sicily">Sicily</A>, <A href="/wiki/Magna_Graecia" title="Magna Graecia">Magna Graecia</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Libya" title="Libya">Libya</A>.\n</P>\n<UL><LI><B>Attica</B>:<SUP id="cite_ref-91" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-91">[86]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Athens" title="Athens">Athens</A>, in the <A href="/wiki/Mystery_religions" class="mw-redirect" title="Mystery religions">mysteries</A> of <A href="/wiki/Agrae" class="mw-redirect" title="Agrae">Agrae</A>. This was a local cult near the river <A href="/wiki/Ilissos" class="mw-redirect" title="Ilissos">Ilissos</A>. They were celebrated during spring in the month <A href="/wiki/Attic_calendar" title="Attic calendar">Anthesterion</A>. Later they became an obligation for the participants of the &quot;greater&quot; <A href="/wiki/Eleusinian_mysteries" class="mw-redirect" title="Eleusinian mysteries">Eleusinian mysteries</A>. There was a temple of Demeter and Kore and an image of <A href="/wiki/Triptolemos" class="mw-redirect" title="Triptolemos">Triptolemos</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-92">[87]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI></UL>\n<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/8/80/Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG/220px-Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG" width="220" height="264" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/8/80/Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG/330px-Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/8/80/Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG 2x" data-file-width="358" data-file-height="430" /></A>  <DIV class="thumbcaption"><DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Demeter_in_horse_chariot_w_daughter_kore_83d40m_wikiC_Tempio_Y_di_Selinunte_sec_VIa.JPG" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>Demeter drives her horse-drawn chariot containing her daughter Persephone at <A href="/wiki/Selinunte" title="Selinunte">Selinunte</A>, <A href="/wiki/Sicily" title="Sicily">Sicily</A> 6th century BC</DIV></DIV></DIV>\n<UL><LI><UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Piraeus" title="Piraeus">Piraeus</A>: The <I>Skirophoria</I>, a festival related to the <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A>.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Megara" title="Megara">Megara</A>: Cult of Demeter <I>thesmophoros</I> and Kore. The city was named after its <I>megara</I> .<SUP id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-93">[88]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Aegina" title="Aegina">Aegina</A>: Cult of Demeter <I>thesmophoros</I> and Kore.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/w/index.php?title=Phlya&amp;action=edit&amp;redlink=1" class="new" title="Phlya (page does not exist)">Phlya</A>, near Koropi, in the <A href="/wiki/Mystery_religions" class="mw-redirect" title="Mystery religions">mysteries</A> of Phlya: These have very old roots and were probably originally dedicated to Demeter <A href="/wiki/Pandora" title="Pandora">Anesidora</A>, Kore, and <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A> Ktesios, who was the god of the underground stored grain. Pausanias mentions a temple of Demeter-Anesidora, Kore <A href="/wiki/Greek_primordial_deities" title="Greek primordial deities">Protogone</A>, and Zeus Ktesios. The surname Protogonos, indicates a later <A href="/wiki/Orphic" class="mw-redirect" title="Orphic">Orphic</A> influence. It seems that the mysteries were related to the mysteries of <A href="/wiki/Andania" title="Andania">Andania</A> in <A href="/wiki/Messene" title="Messene">Messene</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson668_94-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson668-94">[89]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Boeotia</B>:\n<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Ancient_Thebes_(Boeotia)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient Thebes (Boeotia)">Thebes</A>, which Zeus is said to have given to her as an acknowledgement for a favour she had bestowed upon him.<SUP id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-95">[90]</A></SUP> <A href="/wiki/Pausanias_(geographer)" title="Pausanias (geographer)">Pausanias</A> records a grove of <A href="/wiki/Cabeiri" title="Cabeiri">Cabeirian</A> Demeter and the Maid, three miles outside the gates of Thebes, where a ritual was performed, so-called on the grounds that Demeter gave it to the <A href="/wiki/Cabeiri" title="Cabeiri">Cabeiri</A>, who established it at Thebes. The Thebans told Pausanias that some inhabitants of <A href="/wiki/Naupactus" class="mw-redirect" title="Naupactus">Naupactus</A> had performed the same rituals there, and had met with divine vengeance.<SUP id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-96">[91]</A></SUP> The Cabeirian mysteries were introduced from <A href="/wiki/Asia_Minor" class="mw-redirect" title="Asia Minor">Asia Minor</A> at the end of the archaic period. Nothing is known of the older cult, and it seems that the Cabeiri were originally wine-<A href="/wiki/Daemon_(mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Daemon (mythology)">daemons</A>. Inscriptions from the temple in Thebes mention the old one as Cabir, and the new one as son (pais), who are different.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson668_94-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson668-94">[89]</A></SUP> According to Pausanias, Pelarge, the daughter of Potnieus, was connected with the cult of Demeter in the Cabeirian (<A href="/wiki/Potnia" title="Potnia">potniai</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson151_88-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson151-88">[83]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI>A feast in Boeotia, in the month <I>Demetrios</I> (<A href="/wiki/Attic_calendar" title="Attic calendar">Pyanepsion</A>), probably similar with the <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A>.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Ancient_Thebes_(Boeotia)" class="mw-redirect" title="Ancient Thebes (Boeotia)">Thebes</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore in a feast named <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A> but probably different. It was celebrated in the summer month <I>Bukatios</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Diodor_97-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Diodor-97">[92]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Peloponnese</B> (except Arcadia)<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B>Hermione</B>: An old cult of Demeter <A href="/wiki/Chthonic" title="Chthonic">Chthonia</A>, Kore, and <I>Klymenos</I> (<A href="/wiki/Hades" title="Hades">Hades</A>). Cows were pushed into the temple, and then they were killed by four women. It is possible that Hermione was a mythical name, the place of the souls.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Asine" title="Asine">Asine</A>: Cult of Demeter <A href="/wiki/Chthonic" title="Chthonic">Chthonia</A>. The cult seems to be related to the original cult of Demeter in Hermione.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Lakonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Lakonia">Lakonia</A>: Temple of Demeter <I>Eleusinia</I> near <A href="/wiki/Taygetos" class="mw-redirect" title="Taygetos">Taygetos</A>. The feast was named <I>Eleuhinia</I>, and the name was given before the relation of Demeter with the cult of <A href="/wiki/Eleusis" title="Eleusis">Eleusis</A>.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Lakonia" class="mw-redirect" title="Lakonia">Lakonia</A> at Aigila: Dedicated to Demeter. Men were excluded.</LI>\n<LI>near <A href="/wiki/Sparta" title="Sparta">Sparta</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, the Demeters (Δαμάτερες, &quot;Damaters&quot;). According to Hesychius, the feast lasted three days (Thesmophoria).</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Corinth" title="Corinth">Corinth</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Pluton.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Triphylia" title="Triphylia">Triphylia</A> in <A href="/wiki/Elis" title="Elis">Elis</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Hades.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Pellene" title="Pellene">Pellene</A>: Dedicated to the <I>Mysian</I> Demeter. Men were excluded. The next day, men and women became naked.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Andania" title="Andania">Andania</A> in <A href="/wiki/Messenia" title="Messenia">Messenia</A> (near the borders of Arcadia): Cult of the Great goddesses, Demeter and <I>Hagne</I>. Hagne, a goddess of the spring, was the original deity before Demeter. The temple was built near a spring.</LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Arcadia</B><SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson478_26-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson478-26">[23]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Pheneos" class="mw-redirect" title="Pheneos">Pheneos</A>\xa0: Mysteries of Demeter <I>Thesmia</I> and Demeter <I>Eleusinia</I>. The Eleusinian cult was introduced later. The priest took the <I>holy book</I> from a natural cleft. He used the mask of Demeter <I>Kidaria</I>, and he hit his stick on the earth, in a kind of agrarian magic. An Arcadian dance was named kidaris.</LI>\n<LI><B>Pallantion</B> near <A href="/wiki/Tripoli,_Greece" title="Tripoli, Greece">Tripoli</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Karyai_(ancient_city)" class="mw-redirect" title="Karyai (ancient city)">Karyai</A>: Cult of Kore and Pluton.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Tegea" title="Tegea">Tegea</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, the <I>Karpophoroi</I>, &quot;Fruit givers&quot;.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Megalopolis,_Greece" title="Megalopolis, Greece">Megalopolis</A>: Cult of the Great goddesses, Demeter and <I>Kore Sotira</I>, &quot;the savior&quot;.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Mantineia" title="Mantineia">Mantineia</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore in the fest <I>Koragia</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-98">[93]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Trapezus,_Arcadia" title="Trapezus, Arcadia">Trapezus</A>: Mysteries of the Great goddesses, Demeter and Kore. The temple was built near a spring, and a fire was burning out of the earth.</LI>\n<LI>near <A href="/wiki/Thelpusa" title="Thelpusa">Thelpusa</A> in Onkeion: Temple of Demeter Erinys (vengeful) and Demeter Lusia (bathing). In the myth Demeter was united with <A href="/wiki/Poseidon" title="Poseidon">Poseidon Hippios</A> (horse) and bore the horse <A href="/wiki/Arion_(mythology)" title="Arion (mythology)">Arion</A> and the unnamed. The name <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A> was given in West Arcadia.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Phigalia" title="Phigalia">Phigalia</A>: Cult of the mare-headed Demeter (black), and <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A>. Demeter was depicted in her archaic form, a Medusa type with a horse&#39;s head with snaky hair, holding a dove and a dolphin.<SUP id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-99">[94]</A></SUP> The temple was built near a spring.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Lycosura" title="Lycosura">Lycosura</A>,<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A></DIV> Cult of Demeter and <A href="/wiki/Despoina" title="Despoina">Despoina</A>. In the portico of the temple of Despoina there was a tablet with the inscriptions of the mysteries. In front of the temple there was an altar to Demeter and another to Despoine, after which was one of the Great Mother. By the sides stood <A href="/wiki/Artemis" title="Artemis">Artemis</A> and <A href="/wiki/Anytos" title="Anytos">Anytos</A>, the Titan who brought up Despoine. Besides the temple, there was also a hall where the Arcadians celebrated the mysteries<SUP id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-100">[95]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-101">[96]</A></SUP> A fire was always burning in front of the temple of <A href="/wiki/Pan_(mythology)" class="mw-redirect" title="Pan (mythology)">Pan</A> (the goat-god), the god of the wild, shepherds and flocks. In a relief appear dancing animal-headed women (or with animal-masks) in a procession. Near the temple have been found terracotta figures with human bodies, and heads of animals.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson478_26-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson478-26">[23]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Islands</B>\n<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Paros" title="Paros">Paros</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Zeus-Eubuleus.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Amorgos" title="Amorgos">Amorgos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Zeus-Eubuleus.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Delos" title="Delos">Delos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Zeus-Eubuleus. Probably a different feast with the name <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A>, celebrated in a summer month (the same month in Thebes). Two big loaves of bread were oferred to the two goddesses. Another feast was named <I>Megalartia</I>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-Diodor_97-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Diodor-97">[92]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Mykonos" title="Mykonos">Mykonos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and <A href="/wiki/Zeus" title="Zeus">Zeus</A>-Buleus.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Crete" title="Crete">Crete</A>\xa0: Cult of Demeter and Kore, in the month Thesmophorios.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Rhodes" title="Rhodes">Rhodes</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, in the month Thesmophorios. The two goddesses are the Damaters in an inscription from <A href="/wiki/Lindos" title="Lindos">Lindos</A></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Asia_Minor" class="mw-redirect" title="Asia Minor">Asia Minor</A>\n<UL><LI><A href="/wiki/Knidos" title="Knidos">Knidos</A>: Cult of Demeter, Kore, and Pluton.<SUP id="cite_ref-Rhode206_21-13" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Rhode206-21">[18]</A></SUP> Agrarian magic similar to the one used in <A href="/wiki/Thesmophoria" title="Thesmophoria">Thesmophoria</A> and in the cult of the <A href="/wiki/Potnia" title="Potnia">potniai</A> (<A href="/wiki/Cabeiri" title="Cabeiri">Cabeirian</A>).<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Ephesos" class="mw-redirect" title="Ephesos">Ephesos</A>\xa0: Cult of Demeter and Kore, celebrated at night-time.<SUP id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-102">[97]</A></SUP></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Priene" title="Priene">Priene</A>: Cult of Demeter and Kore, similar to the Thesmophoria.<SUP id="cite_ref-Nilsson463_25-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Nilsson463-25">[22]</A></SUP></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Sicily" title="Sicily">Sicily</A></LI></UL>\n<DIV class="thumb tright"><DIV class="thumbinner" T. Murray, trans)</LI>\n<LI>&quot;<A href="/wiki/Althea" title="Althea">Althea</A> prayed instantly to the gods, being grieved for her brother&#39;s slaying; and furthermore instantly beat with her hands upon the all-nurturing earth, calling upon Hades and dread Persephone&quot; (9, 569)</LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Odyssey</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;And come to the house of Hades and dread Persephone to seek sooth saying of the spirit of Theban Teiresias. To him even in death Persephone has granted reason that\xa0...&quot; (book 10, card 473)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Hymn" title="Hymn">Hymns to</A> <A href="/wiki/Demeter" title="Demeter">Demeter</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B>Hymn 2</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;Mistress Demeter goddess of heaven, which God or mortal man has rapt away Persephone and pierced with sorrow your dear heart?<I>(hymn 2, card 40)</I></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Hymn 13</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;I start to sing for Demeter the lovely-faced goddess, for her and her daughter the most beautiful Persephone. Hail goddess keep this city safe!&quot; (hymn 13, card 1)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Pindar" title="Pindar">Pindar</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B> Olympian</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;Now go Echo, to the dark-walled home of Persephone.&quot;(book O, poem 14)</LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Isthmean</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;Aecus showed them the way to the house of Persephone and nymphs, one of them carrying a ball.&quot;(book 1, poem 8)</LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Nemean</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;Island which Zeus, the lord of Olympus gave to Persephone;he nodded descent with his flowers hair.&quot;(book N, poem 1)</LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Pythian</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;You splendor-loving city, most beautiful on earth, home of Persephone. You who inhabit the hill of well-built dwellings.&quot;(book P, poem 12)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Aeschylus" title="Aeschylus">Aeschylus</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B>Libation bearers</B>:\n<UL><LI>Electra:&quot;O Persephone, grant us indeed a glorious victory!&quot; (card 479)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Aristophanes" title="Aristophanes">Aristophanes</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B>Thesmophoriazusae</B>:\n<UL><LI>Mnesilochos:&quot;Thou Mistress Demeter, the most valuable friend and thou Persephone, grant that I may be able to offer you!&quot; (card 266)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Euripides" title="Euripides">Euripides</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B>Alcestis</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;O you brave and best hail, sitting as attendand Beside&#39;s Hades bride Persephone!&quot; (card 741)</LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><B>Hecuba</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;It is said that any of the dead that stand beside Persephone, that the Danaids have left the plains to Troy.&quot; (card 130)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Bacchylides" title="Bacchylides">Bacchylides</A><SUP id="cite_ref-perseus_105-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-perseus-105">[100]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B> Epinicians</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;Flashing thunderbolt went down to the halls of slender-ankled Persephone to bring up into the light of Hades.&quot; (book Ep. poem 5)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Vergil" class="mw-redirect" title="Vergil">Vergil</A><SUP id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-106">[101]</A></SUP>\n<UL><LI><B>The Aeneid</B>:\n<UL><LI>&quot;For since she had not died through fate, or by a well-earned death, but wretchedly, before her time, inflamed with sudden madness, Proserpine had not yet taken a lock of golden hair from her head, or condemned her soul to Stygian Orcus.&quot; (IV.696–99)</LI></UL></LI></UL></LI></UL>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Modern_reception">Modern reception</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Persephone&amp;action=edit&amp;section=20" title="Edit section: Modern reception">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/Persephone_in_popular_culture" title="Persephone in popular culture">Persephone in popular culture</A></DIV>\n<P>In 1934, <A href="/wiki/Igor_Stravinsky" title="Igor Stravinsky">Igor Stravinsky</A> based his <A href="/wiki/Melodrama" title="Melodrama">melodrama</A> <I><A href="/wiki/Pers%C3%A9phone_(Stravinsky)" title="Perséphone (Stravinsky)">Perséphone</A></I> on Persephone&#39;s story. In 1961, Frederick Ashton of the Royal Ballet appropriated Stravinsky&#39;s score, to choreograph a ballet starring Svetlana Beriosova as Persephone.\n</P><P>Persephone also appears many times in popular culture. Featured in a variety of young adult novels such as &quot;Persephone&quot;<SUP id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-107">[102]</A></SUP> by Kaitlin Bevis, &quot;Persephone&#39;s Orchard&quot;<SUP id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-108">[103]</A></SUP> by Molly Ringle, &quot;The Goddess Test&quot; by Aimee Carter, &quot;The Goddess Letters&quot; by Carol Orlock, and &quot;Abandon&quot; by Meg Cabot, her story has also been treated by Suzanne Banay Santo in &quot;Persephone Under the Earth&quot; in the light of women&#39;s spirituality. Here Santo treats the mythic elements in terms of maternal sacrifice to the burgeoning sexuality of an adolescent daughter. Accompanied by the classic, sensual paintings of Frederic Lord Leighton and William-Adolphe Bouguereau, Santo portrays Persephone not as a victim but as a woman in quest of sexual depth and power, transcending the role of daughter, though ultimately returning to it as an awakened Queen.<SUP id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-109">[104]</A></SUP>\n</P>\n<H2><SPAN id="content" class="mw-body" role="main">\n\t\t\t<A id="top"></A>\n\t\t\t<DIV id="siteNotice" class="mw-body-content"><DIV id="centralNotice"></DIV><!-- CentralNotice --></DIV><DIV class="mw-indicators mw-body-content">\n</DIV>\n<H1 id="firstHeading" class="firstHeading" lang="en">Colony (biology)</H1>\t\t\t<DIV id="bodyContent" class="mw-body-content">\n\t\t\t\t<DIV id="siteSub" class="noprint">From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia</DIV>\t\t\t\t<DIV id="contentSub"></DIV>\n\t\t\t\t\t\t\t\t<DIV id="jump-to-nav" class="mw-jump">\n\t\t\t\t\tJump to:\t\t\t\t\t<A href="#mw-head">navigation</A>, \t\t\t\t\t<A href="#p-search">search</A>\n\t\t\t\t</DIV>\n\t\t\t\t<DIV id="mw-content-text" lang="en" dir="ltr" class="mw-content-ltr"><DIV class="mw-parser-output"><P>In <A href="/wiki/Biology" title="Biology">biology</A>, a <B>colony</B> is composed of two or more <A href="/wiki/Conspecific" class="mw-redirect" title="Conspecific">conspecific</A> individuals living in close association with, or connected to, one another. This association is usually for mutual benefit such as stronger defense or the ability to attack bigger prey.<SUP id="cite_ref-Jackson1977_1-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Jackson1977-1">[1]</A></SUP> It is a cluster of identical cells (clones) on the surface of (or within) a solid medium, usually derived from a single parent cell, as in bacterial colony.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> In contrast, a <A href="/wiki/Solitary_animal" title="Solitary animal">solitary organism</A> is one in which all individuals live independently and have all of the functions needed to survive and reproduce.</P>\n<P>Colonies, in the context of development, may be composed of two or more unitary (or solitary) organisms or be <A href="/wiki/Modular" class="mw-redirect" title="Modular">modular</A> organisms. <B>Unitary organisms</B> have determinate development (set life stages) from <A href="/wiki/Zygote" title="Zygote">zygote</A> to adult form and individuals or groups of individuals (colonies) are visually distinct. <B>Modular organisms</B> have indeterminate growth forms (life stages not set) through repeated iteration of genetically identical modules (or individuals), and it can be difficult to distinguish between the colony as a whole and the modules within.<SUP id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-3">[3]</A></SUP> In the latter case, modules may have specific functions within the colony.</P>\n<P>Some organisms are primarily independent and form <A href="/wiki/Facultative" title="Facultative">facultative</A> colonies in reply to environmental conditions while others must live in a colony to survive (<A href="/wiki/Obligate" title="Obligate">obligate</A>). For example, some <A href="/wiki/Carpenter_bee" title="Carpenter bee">carpenter bees</A> will form colonies when a dominant hierarchy is formed between two or more nest foundresses<SUP id="cite_ref-DunnRichards2003_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-DunnRichards2003-4">[4]</A></SUP> (facultative colony), while <A href="/wiki/Coral" title="Coral">corals</A> are animals that are physically connected by living tissue (the <A href="/wiki/Coenosarc" title="Coenosarc">coenosarc</A>) that contains a shared <A href="/wiki/Gastrovascular_cavity" title="Gastrovascular cavity">gastrovascular cavity</A>.</P>\n<P></P>\n<DIV id="toc" class="toc">\n<DIV class="toctitle" lang="en" dir="ltr" xml:lang="en">\n<H2>Contents</H2>\n<SPAN class="toctoggle">\xa0[<A role="button" tabindex="0" class="togglelink">hide</A>]\xa0</SPAN></DIV>\n<UL>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-1"><A href="#Colony_types"><SPAN class="tocnumber">1</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Colony types</SPAN></A>\n<UL>\n<LI class="toclevel-2 tocsection-2"><A href="#Social_colonies"><SPAN class="tocnumber">1.1</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Social colonies</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-2 tocsection-3"><A href="#Modular_organisms"><SPAN class="tocnumber">1.2</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Modular organisms</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-2 tocsection-4"><A href="#Microbial_colonies"><SPAN class="tocnumber">1.3</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Microbial colonies</SPAN></A></LI>\n</UL>\n</LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-5"><A href="#Life_history"><SPAN class="tocnumber">2</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Life history</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-6"><A href="#See_also"><SPAN class="tocnumber">3</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">See also</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-7"><A href="#References"><SPAN class="tocnumber">4</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">References</SPAN></A></LI>\n</UL>\n</DIV>\n<P></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Colony_types">Colony types</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: Colony types">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Social_colonies">Social colonies</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Social colonies">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>\n<DIV class="thumb tright">\n<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg/220px-Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg/330px-Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg/440px-Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1248" data-file-height="830" /></A>\n<DIV class="thumbcaption">\n<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Colony_Northern_Gannet_Morus_bassanus.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>\nA breeding colony of <A href="/wiki/Northern_gannet" title="Northern gannet">Northern gannets</A> on the <A href="/wiki/Heligoland" title="Heligoland">Heligoland</A> archipelago in the <A href="/wiki/North_Sea" title="North Sea">North Sea</A>.</DIV>\n</DIV>\n</DIV>\n<P><A href="/wiki/Unicellular" class="mw-redirect" title="Unicellular">Unicellular</A> and <A href="/wiki/Multicellular" class="mw-redirect" title="Multicellular">multicellular</A> unitary organisms may aggregate to form colonies. For example,</P>\n<UL>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Protist" title="Protist">Protists</A> such as <A href="/wiki/Slime_mold" title="Slime mold">slime molds</A> are many unicellular organisms that aggregate to form colonies when food resources are hard to come by, as together they are more reactive to chemical cues released by preferred prey.</LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Eusociality" title="Eusociality">Eusocial</A> insects like <A href="/wiki/Ant" title="Ant">ants</A> and <A href="/wiki/Honey_bee" title="Honey bee">honey bees</A> are multicellular animals that live in colonies with a highly organized social structure. Colonies of some social insects may be deemed <A href="/wiki/Superorganism" title="Superorganism">superorganisms</A>.</LI>\n<LI>Animals such as <A href="/wiki/Human" title="Human">humans</A> and <A href="/wiki/Rodent" title="Rodent">rodents</A> form breeding or <A href="/wiki/Bird_colony" title="Bird colony">nesting colonies</A>, potentially for more successful mating and to better protect offspring.\n<UL>\n<LI>The <A href="/wiki/Bracken_Cave" title="Bracken Cave">Bracken Cave</A> is the summer home to a colony of around 20 million <A href="/wiki/Mexican_free-tailed_bat" title="Mexican free-tailed bat">Mexican free-tailed bats</A> making it the largest known concentration of mammals.<SUP id="cite_ref-natgeo_5-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-natgeo-5">[5]</A></SUP></LI>\n</UL>\n</LI>\n</UL>\n<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Modular_organisms">Modular organisms</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Modular organisms">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>\n<P>Modular organisms are those in which a genet (or genetic individual formed from a <A href="/wiki/Sexual_reproduction" title="Sexual reproduction">sexually-produced</A> <A href="/wiki/Zygote" title="Zygote">zygote</A>) asexually reproduces to form genetically identical clones called <A href="/wiki/Ramet" class="mw-redirect" title="Ramet">ramets</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Winston2010_6-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Winston2010-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>A <B><A href="/wiki/Clonal_colony" title="Clonal colony">clonal colony</A></B> is when the ramets of a genet live in close proximity or are physically connected. Ramets may have all of the functions needed to survive on their own or be interdependent on other ramets. For example, some <A href="/wiki/Sea_anemone" title="Sea anemone">sea anemones</A> go through the process of pedal laceration in which a genetically identical individual is asexually produced from tissue broken off from the anemone&#39;s pedal disc. In plants, clonal colonies are created through the propagation of genetically identical trees by <A href="/wiki/Stolon" title="Stolon">stolons</A> or <A href="/wiki/Rhizome" title="Rhizome">rhizomes</A>.</P>\n<P><B>Colonial organisms</B> are <A href="/wiki/Clonal_colonies" class="mw-redirect" title="Clonal colonies">clonal colonies</A> composed of many physically connected, interdependent individuals. Colonial organisms can be unicellular, as in the alga <I><A href="/wiki/Volvox" title="Volvox">Volvox</A></I> (a <A href="/wiki/Coenobium_(morphology)" title="Coenobium (morphology)">coenobium</A>), or <A href="/wiki/Multicellular_organism" title="Multicellular organism">multicellular</A>, as in the <A href="/wiki/Phylum" title="Phylum">phylum</A> <A href="/wiki/Bryozoa" title="Bryozoa">Bryozoa</A>. The former type may have been the first step toward multicellular <A href="/wiki/Organism" title="Organism">organisms</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP> Individuals within a multicellular colonial organism may be called <A href="/wiki/Ramet" class="mw-redirect" title="Ramet">ramets</A>, <A href="/wiki/Modularity_(biology)" title="Modularity (biology)">modules</A>, or <A href="/wiki/Zooid" title="Zooid">zooids</A>. Structural and functional variation (<A href="/wiki/Polymorphism_(biology)" title="Polymorphism (biology)">polymorphism</A>), when present, designates ramet responsibilities such as feeding, reproduction, and defense. To that end, being physically connected allows the colonial organism to distribute nutrients and energy obtained by feeding zooids throughout the colony. An example of colonial organisms that is well known are hydrozoans, like Portuguese man o&#39; wars.<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP></P>\n<H3><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Microbial_colonies">Microbial colonies</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: Microbial colonies">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H3>\n<P>A <B>microbial colony</B> is defined as a visible cluster of <A href="/wiki/Microorganism" title="Microorganism">microorganisms</A> growing on the surface of or within a solid medium, presumably cultured from a single cell.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> Because the colony is <A href="/wiki/Clone_(cell_biology)" title="Clone (cell biology)">clonal</A>, with all organisms in it descending from a single ancestor (assuming no <A href="/wiki/Contamination" title="Contamination">contamination</A>), they are genetically identical, except for any <A href="/wiki/Mutation" title="Mutation">mutations</A> (which occur at low frequencies). Obtaining such genetically identical organisms (or pure <A href="/wiki/Strain_(biology)" title="Strain (biology)">strains</A>) can be useful; this is done by spreading organisms on a culture plate and starting a new stock from a single resulting colony.</P>\n<P>A <B><A href="/wiki/Biofilm" title="Biofilm">biofilm</A></B> is a colony of <A href="/wiki/Microorganism" title="Microorganism">microorganisms</A> often comprising several species, with properties and capabilities greater than the aggregate of capabilities of the individual organisms.</P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Life_history">Life history</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: Life history">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<P>Individuals in social colonies and modular organisms receive benefit to such a lifestyle. For example, it may be easier to seek out food, defend a nesting site, or increase competitive ability against other species. Modular organisms&#39; ability to reproduce asexually in addition to sexually allows them unique benefits that social colonies do not have.<SUP id="cite_ref-Winston2010_6-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Winston2010-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>The energy required for sexual reproduction varies based on the frequency and length of reproductive activity, number and size of offspring, and parental care.<SUP id="cite_ref-KunzOrrell_10-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-KunzOrrell-10">[10]</A></SUP> While solitary individuals bear all of those energy costs, individuals in some social colonies share a portion of those costs.</P>\n<P>Modular organisms save energy by using asexual reproduction during their life. Energy reserved in this way allows them to put more energy towards colony growth, regenerating lost modules (due to predation or other cause of death), or response to environmental conditions.</P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="See_also">See also</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Colony_(biology)&amp;action=edit&amp;section=6" title="Edit section: See also">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<TABLE role="presentation" For other uses, see <A href="/wiki/Tradewind_(disambiguation)" class="mw-redirect mw-disambig" title="Tradewind (disambiguation)">Tradewind</A>.</DIV>\n<DIV class="thumb tright">\n<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:302px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png/300px-Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png" width="300" height="132" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png/450px-Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png/600px-Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png 2x" data-file-width="1425" data-file-height="625" /></A>\n<DIV class="thumbcaption">\n<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Map_prevailing_winds_on_earth.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>\nThe <A href="/wiki/Westerlies" title="Westerlies">westerlies</A> (blue arrows) and trade winds (yellow and brown arrows)</DIV>\n</DIV>\n</DIV>\n<P>The <B>trade winds</B> are the <A href="/wiki/Prevailing_winds" title="Prevailing winds">prevailing pattern</A> of easterly surface <A href="/wiki/Wind" title="Wind">winds</A> found in the <A href="/wiki/Tropics" title="Tropics">tropics</A>, within the lower portion of the <A href="/wiki/Earth%27s_atmosphere" class="mw-redirect" title="Earth&#39;s atmosphere">Earth&#39;s atmosphere</A>, in the lower section of the <A href="/wiki/Troposphere" title="Troposphere">troposphere</A> near the Earth&#39;s <A href="/wiki/Equator" title="Equator">equator</A>. The trade winds blow predominantly from the northeast in the <A href="/wiki/Northern_Hemisphere" title="Northern Hemisphere">Northern Hemisphere</A> and from the southeast in the <A href="/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere" title="Southern Hemisphere">Southern Hemisphere</A>, strengthening during the winter and when the <A href="/wiki/Arctic_oscillation" title="Arctic oscillation">Arctic oscillation</A> is in its warm phase. Trade winds have been used by captains of <A href="/wiki/Sailing_ship" title="Sailing ship">sailing ships</A> to cross the world&#39;s oceans for centuries, and enabled <A href="/wiki/Colonial_empire" title="Colonial empire">European empire</A> expansion into the Americas and trade routes to become established across the <A href="/wiki/Atlantic_ocean" class="mw-redirect" title="Atlantic ocean">Atlantic</A> and <A href="/wiki/Pacific_ocean" class="mw-redirect" title="Pacific ocean">Pacific oceans</A>.</P>\n<P>In <A href="/wiki/Meteorology" title="Meteorology">meteorology</A>, the trade winds act as the <A href="/wiki/Prevailing_winds" title="Prevailing winds">steering flow</A> for <A href="/wiki/Tropical_storms" class="mw-redirect" title="Tropical storms">tropical storms</A> that form over the Atlantic, Pacific, and southern <A href="/wiki/Indian_Ocean" title="Indian Ocean">Indian Oceans</A> and make landfall in North America, Southeast Asia, and Madagascar and eastern Africa, respectively. Trade winds also transport African dust westward across the <A href="/wiki/Atlantic_Ocean" title="Atlantic Ocean">Atlantic Ocean</A> into the <A href="/wiki/Caribbean_Sea" title="Caribbean Sea">Caribbean Sea</A>, as well as portions of southeastern <A href="/wiki/North_America" title="North America">North America</A>. Shallow <A href="/wiki/Cumulus_cloud" title="Cumulus cloud">cumulus clouds</A> are seen within trade wind regimes, and are capped from becoming taller by a trade wind inversion, which is caused by descending air aloft from within the <A href="/wiki/Subtropical_ridge" title="Subtropical ridge">subtropical ridge</A>. The weaker the trade winds become, the more rainfall can be expected in the neighboring landmasses.</P>\n<P></P>\n<DIV id="toc" class="toc">\n<DIV class="toctitle">\n<H2>Contents</H2>\n<SPAN class="toctoggle">\xa0[<A role="button" tabindex="0" class="togglelink">hide</A>]\xa0</SPAN></DIV>\n<UL>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-1"><A href="#History"><SPAN class="tocnumber">1</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">History</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-2"><A href="#Cause"><SPAN class="tocnumber">2</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Cause</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-3"><A href="#Weather_effects"><SPAN class="tocnumber">3</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Weather effects</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-4"><A href="#See_also"><SPAN class="tocnumber">4</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">See also</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-5"><A href="#References"><SPAN class="tocnumber">5</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">References</SPAN></A></LI>\n</UL>\n</DIV>\n<P></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="History">History</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Trade_winds&amp;action=edit&amp;section=1" title="Edit section: History">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<DIV class="thumb tright">\n<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:202px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Spanish_Galleon.jpg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Spanish_Galleon.jpg/200px-Spanish_Galleon.jpg" width="200" height="275" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/08/Spanish_Galleon.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="300" data-file-height="412" /></A>\n<DIV class="thumbcaption">\n<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Spanish_Galleon.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>\nA Spanish galleon</DIV>\n</DIV>\n</DIV>\n<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Discovery" title="Age of Discovery">Age of Discovery</A>, <A href="/wiki/Volta_do_Mar" class="mw-redirect" title="Volta do Mar">Volta do Mar</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Age_of_sail" class="mw-redirect" title="Age of sail">Age of sail</A></DIV>\n<P>The term <I>trade winds</I> originally derives from the early fourteenth century late <A href="/wiki/Middle_English" title="Middle English">Middle English</A> word &#39;trade,&#39; meaning &quot;path&quot; or &quot;track.&quot;<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> The Portuguese recognized the importance of the trade winds (then the <I><A href="/wiki/Volta_do_mar" title="Volta do mar">Volta do mar</A></I>, meaning in Portuguese &quot;turn of the sea&quot; but also &quot;return from the sea&quot;) in navigation in both the north and south Atlantic ocean as early as the 15th century.<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> From West Africa, the Portuguese had to sail away from continental Portugal, that is, to west and northwest. They could then turn northeast, to the area around the <A href="/wiki/Azores" title="Azores">Azores</A> islands, and finally east to mainland Europe. They also learned that to reach South Africa, they needed to go far out in the ocean, head for Brazil, and around 30°S go east again. Following the African coast southbound means upwind in the Southern hemisphere. In the Pacific ocean, the full wind circulation, which included both the trade wind easterlies and higher-latitude <A href="/wiki/Westerlies" title="Westerlies">Westerlies</A>, was unknown to Europeans until <A href="/wiki/Andres_de_Urdaneta" class="mw-redirect" title="Andres de Urdaneta">Andres de Urdaneta</A>&#39;s voyage in 1565.<SUP id="cite_ref-pg18_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pg18-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>The captain of a sailing ship seeks a course along which the winds can be expected to blow in the direction of travel.<SUP id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-4">[4]</A></SUP> During the <A href="/wiki/Age_of_Sail" title="Age of Sail">Age of Sail</A>, the pattern of <A href="/wiki/Prevailing_winds" title="Prevailing winds">prevailing winds</A> made various points of the globe easy or difficult to access, and therefore had a direct effect on European empire-building and thus on modern political geography. For example, <A href="/wiki/Manila_galleon" title="Manila galleon">Manila galleons</A> could not sail into the wind at all.<SUP id="cite_ref-pg18_3-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pg18-3">[3]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>By the 18th century the importance of the trade winds to England&#39;s merchant fleet for crossing the Atlantic Ocean had led both the general public and etymologists to identify the name with a later meaning of &#39;trade&#39;, &quot;(foreign) commerce&quot;.<SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP> Between 1847 and 1849, <A href="/wiki/Matthew_Fontaine_Maury" title="Matthew Fontaine Maury">Matthew Fontaine Maury</A> collected enough information to create wind and current charts for the world&#39;s oceans.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cause">Cause</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Trade_winds&amp;action=edit&amp;section=2" title="Edit section: Cause">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<DIV class="thumb tright">\n<DIV class="thumbinner" style="width:402px;"><A href="/wiki/File:Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg" class="image"><IMG alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg/400px-Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg.png" width="400" height="334" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg/600px-Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg/800px-Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="1000" data-file-height="835" /></A>\n<DIV class="thumbcaption">\n<DIV class="magnify"><A href="/wiki/File:Earth_Global_Circulation_-_en.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></A></DIV>\n3D map showing <A href="/wiki/Hadley_cell" title="Hadley cell">Hadley cells</A> in relationship to trade winds on the surface.</DIV>\n</DIV>\n</DIV>\n<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <A href="/wiki/Air_mass" title="Air mass">Air mass</A>, <A href="/wiki/Hadley_cell" title="Hadley cell">Hadley cell</A>, <A href="/wiki/Humidity" title="Humidity">Humidity</A>, <A href="/wiki/Intertropical_Convergence_Zone" title="Intertropical Convergence Zone">Intertropical Convergence Zone</A>, <A href="/wiki/Monsoon" title="Monsoon">Monsoon</A>, <A href="/wiki/Monsoon_trough" title="Monsoon trough">Monsoon trough</A>, <A href="/wiki/Near-equatorial_trough" class="mw-redirect" title="Near-equatorial trough">Near-equatorial trough</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Prevailing_winds" title="Prevailing winds">Prevailing winds</A></DIV>\n<P>As part of the <A href="/wiki/Hadley_cell" title="Hadley cell">Hadley cell</A> circulation, surface air flows toward the equator while the flow aloft is towards the <A href="/wiki/Geographic_pole" class="mw-redirect" title="Geographic pole">poles</A>. A <A href="/wiki/Low-pressure_area" title="Low-pressure area">low-pressure area</A> of calm, light variable winds near the equator is known as the <A href="/wiki/Doldrums" title="Doldrums">doldrums</A>,<SUP id="cite_ref-dold_7-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-dold-7">[7]</A></SUP> near-equatorial trough,<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> intertropical front, or the <A href="/wiki/Intertropical_Convergence_Zone" title="Intertropical Convergence Zone">Intertropical Convergence Zone</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP> When located within a <A href="/wiki/Monsoon" title="Monsoon">monsoon</A> region, this zone of low pressure and wind convergence is also known as the <A href="/wiki/Monsoon_trough" title="Monsoon trough">monsoon trough</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-10" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-10">[10]</A></SUP> Around 30° in both hemispheres, air begins to descend toward the surface in subtropical high-pressure belts known as <A href="/wiki/Subtropical_ridge" title="Subtropical ridge">subtropical ridges</A>. The subsident (sinking) air is relatively dry because as it descends, the temperature increases, but the absolute humidity remains constant, which lowers the relative humidity of the air mass. This warm, dry air is known as a superior air mass and normally resides above a maritime tropical (warm and moist) air mass. An increase of temperature with height is known as a temperature inversion. When it occurs within a trade wind regime, it is known as a trade wind inversion.<SUP id="cite_ref-11" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-11">[11]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>The surface air that flows from these subtropical high-pressure belts toward the Equator is deflected toward the west in both hemispheres by the <A href="/wiki/Coriolis_effect" class="mw-redirect" title="Coriolis effect">Coriolis effect</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-12" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-12">[12]</A></SUP> These winds blow predominantly from the northeast in the <A href="/wiki/Northern_Hemisphere" title="Northern Hemisphere">Northern Hemisphere</A> and from the southeast in the <A href="/wiki/Southern_Hemisphere" title="Southern Hemisphere">Southern Hemisphere</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-Ralph_13-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-Ralph-13">[13]</A></SUP> Because winds are named for the direction from which the wind is blowing,<SUP id="cite_ref-HOWTOREAD_14-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-HOWTOREAD-14">[14]</A></SUP> these winds are called the northeasterly trade winds in the Northern Hemisphere and the southeasterly trade winds in the Southern Hemisphere. The trade winds of both hemispheres meet at the <A href="/wiki/Doldrums" title="Doldrums">doldrums</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-dold_7-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-dold-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>As they blow across tropical regions, air masses heat up over lower latitudes due to more direct sunlight. Those that develop over land (continental) are drier and hotter than those that develop over oceans (maritime), and travel northward on the western periphery of the subtropical ridge.<SUP id="cite_ref-15" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-15">[15]</A></SUP> Maritime tropical air masses are sometimes referred to as trade air masses.<SUP id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-16">[16]</A></SUP> The one region of the <A href="/wiki/Earth" title="Earth">Earth</A> which has an absence of trade winds is the north <A href="/wiki/Indian_ocean" class="mw-redirect" title="Indian ocean">Indian ocean</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-17">[17]</A></SUP></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Weather_effects">Weather effects</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Trade_winds&amp;action=edit&amp;section=3" title="Edit section: Weather effects">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<P>Clouds which form above regions within trade wind regimes are typically composed of cumulus which extend no more than 4 kilometres (13,000\xa0ft) in height, and are capped from being taller by the trade wind inversion.<SUP id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-18">[18]</A></SUP> Trade winds originate more from the direction of the poles (northeast in the Northern Hemisphere, southeast in the Southern Hemisphere) during the cold season, and are stronger in the winter than the summer.<SUP id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-19">[19]</A></SUP> As an example, the windy season in the <A href="/wiki/Guyana" title="Guyana">Guianas</A>, which lie at low latitudes in <A href="/wiki/South_America" title="South America">South America</A>, occurs between January and April.<SUP id="cite_ref-20" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-20">[20]</A></SUP> When the phase of the <A href="/wiki/Arctic_oscillation" title="Arctic oscillation">Arctic oscillation</A> (AO) is warm, trade winds are stronger within the tropics. The cold phase of the AO leads to weaker trade winds.<SUP id="cite_ref-21" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-21">[21]</A></SUP> When the trade winds are weaker, more extensive areas of rain fall upon landmasses within the tropics, such as <A href="/wiki/Central_America" title="Central America">Central America</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-22">[22]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>During mid-summer in the Northern Hemisphere (July), the westward-moving trade winds south of the northward-moving <A href="/wiki/Subtropical_ridge" title="Subtropical ridge">subtropical ridge</A> expand northwestward from the <A href="/wiki/Caribbean_sea" class="mw-redirect" title="Caribbean sea">Caribbean sea</A> into southeastern North America (Florida and Gulf Coast). When dust from the <A href="/wiki/Sahara" title="Sahara">Sahara</A> moving around the southern periphery of the ridge travels over land, rainfall is suppressed and the sky changes from a blue to a white appearance which leads to an increase in red sunsets. Its presence negatively impacts <A href="/wiki/Air_quality" class="mw-redirect" title="Air quality">air quality</A> by adding to the count of airborne particulates.<SUP id="cite_ref-pooraq_23-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-pooraq-23">[23]</A></SUP> Although the Southeast USA has some of the cleanest air in North America, much of the African dust that reaches the United States affects Florida.<SUP id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-24">[24]</A></SUP> Since 1970, dust outbreaks have worsened due to periods of drought in Africa. There is a large variability in the dust transport to the Caribbean and Florida from year to year.<SUP id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-25">[25]</A></SUP> Dust events have been linked to a decline in the health of <A href="/wiki/Coral_reef" title="Coral reef">coral reefs</A> across the Caribbean and Florida, primarily since the 1970s.<SUP id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-26">[26]</A></SUP></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="See_also">See also</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Trade_winds&amp;action=edit&amp;section=4" title="Edit section: See also">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<UL>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Intertropical_Convergence_Zone" title="Intertropical Convergence Zone">Intertropical Convergence Zone</A></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Winds_in_the_Age_of_Sail" title="Winds in the Age of Sail">Winds in the Age of Sail</A></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Westerly_wind_burst" title="Westerly wind burst">Westerly wind burst</A></LI>\n<LI><A href="/wiki/Volta_do_mar" title="Volta do mar">Volta do mar</A></LI>\n</UL>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="References">References</SPAN><SPAN class="mw-editsection"><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</SPAN><A href="/w/index.php?title=Trade_winds&amp;action=edit&amp;section=5" title="Edit section: References">edit</A><SPAN class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</SPAN></SPAN></H2>\n<DIV class="reflist columns references-column-width" style="-moz-column-width: 30em; -webkit-column-width: 30em; column-width: 30em; list-style-type: decimal;">\n<OL class="references">\n<LI id="cite_note-1"><SPAN class="mw-cite-backlink"><B><A href="#cite_ref-1"><SPAN class="cite-accessibility-label">Jump up </SPAN>^</A></B></SPAN> <SPAN class="reference-text"><CITE class="citation book">Carol G. title="High School Musical">High School Musical</A></I></TD>\n</TR>\n<TR>\n<TH scope="row">Followed by</TH>\n<TD><I><A href="/wiki/High_School_Musical_3:_Senior_Year" title="High School Musical 3: Senior Year">High School Musical 3: Senior Year</A></I></TD>\n</TR>\n</TBODY></TABLE>\n<P><I><B>High School Musical 2</B></I> is the second film in the <A href="/wiki/High_School_Musical_(film_series)" class="mw-redirect" title="High School Musical (film series)"><I>High School Musical</I> series</A>. The World Premiere took place on August 14, 2007,<SUP id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-1">[1]</A></SUP> at Disneyland, in Anaheim, California. The primary cast, including <A href="/wiki/Zac_Efron" title="Zac Efron">Zac Efron</A>, <A href="/wiki/Vanessa_Hudgens" title="Vanessa Hudgens">Vanessa Hudgens</A>, <A href="/wiki/Ashley_Tisdale" title="Ashley Tisdale">Ashley Tisdale</A>, <A href="/wiki/Lucas_Grabeel" title="Lucas Grabeel">Lucas Grabeel</A>, and <A href="/wiki/Corbin_Bleu" title="Corbin Bleu">Corbin Bleu</A> attended the event. The film debuted on television on August 17, 2007, on <A href="/wiki/Disney_Channel" title="Disney Channel">Disney Channel</A> in the U.S., and on <A href="/wiki/Family_Channel_(Canadian_TV_network)" title="Family Channel (Canadian TV network)">Family</A> in Canada.</P>\n<P>In the second installment of the Disney franchise, high school student Troy Bolton stresses over getting a <A href="/wiki/Employment" title="Employment">job</A>, with the price of <A href="/wiki/College" title="College">college</A> expenses looming on his mind, as well as trying to make sure he and Gabriella Montez are able to stay together all summer. This situation attracts the attention of Sharpay Evans, who attempts to steal Troy for herself by hiring him at her family&#39;s country club.</P>\n<P>The premiere was seen by a total of over 17.2 million viewers<SUP id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-2">[2]</A></SUP> in the <A href="/wiki/United_States" title="United States">United States</A> which is almost 10 million more than its predecessor, making it the highest-rated Disney Channel Movie of all time as well as the highest-rated <A href="/wiki/Basic_cable" class="mw-redirect" title="Basic cable">basic cable</A> telecast at the time.<SUP id="cite_ref-patriots_3-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-patriots-3">[3]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-variety_4-0" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-variety-4">[4]</A></SUP><SUP id="cite_ref-5" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-5">[5]</A></SUP></P>\n<P></P>\n<DIV id="toc" class="toc">\n<DIV class="toctitle" lang="en" dir="ltr" xml:lang="en">\n<H2>Contents</H2>\n<SPAN class="toctoggle">\xa0[<A role="button" tabindex="0" class="togglelink">hide</A>]\xa0</SPAN></DIV>\n<UL>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-1"><A href="#Plot"><SPAN class="tocnumber">1</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Plot</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-2"><A href="#Cast"><SPAN class="tocnumber">2</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Cast</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-3"><A href="#Release"><SPAN class="tocnumber">3</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Release</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-4"><A href="#Songs"><SPAN class="tocnumber">4</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Songs</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-5"><A href="#Reception"><SPAN class="tocnumber">5</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Reception</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-6"><A href="#High_School_Musical_2:_On_Stage!"><SPAN class="tocnumber">6</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">High School Musical 2: On Stage!</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-7"><A href="#Awards"><SPAN class="tocnumber">7</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">Awards</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-8"><A href="#References"><SPAN class="tocnumber">8</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">References</SPAN></A></LI>\n<LI class="toclevel-1 tocsection-9"><A href="#External_links"><SPAN class="tocnumber">9</SPAN> <SPAN class="toctext">External links</SPAN></A></LI>\n</UL>\n</DIV>\n<P></P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Plot">Plot</SPAN></H2>\n<P>The school year ends with everyone at East High School looking forward to summer vacation (&quot;What Time Is It&quot;). Troy Bolton is still dating Gabriella Montez, who decides to stay in <A href="/wiki/Albuquerque,_New_Mexico" title="Albuquerque, New Mexico">Albuquerque</A> with her mother. Troy eventually decides to look for a summer job to gain money for college.</P>\n<P>Sharpay and Ryan Evans plan to spend part of the summer at their family&#39;s country club, Lava Springs (&quot;Fabulous&quot;), but Sharpay&#39;s summer plans also include pursuing Troy, whom she has arranged to be hired at the club. However, Troy convinces the club&#39;s manager, Mr. Fulton, into hiring Gabriella and their close group of friends as well; including Taylor and Chad. Sharpay is enraged upon learning that Gabriella is working as one of the lifeguards, but is unable to get her fired. So she orders Fulton to give them difficult tasks so they would be best to quit. Fulton attempts to intimidate the group, but Troy rebuilds their confidence and convinces them that they can persevere (&quot;Work This Out&quot;).</P>\n<P>Troy continues to worry about funding for college. Sharpay senses his need and arranges for Troy to be promoted, hoping that this will convince him to sing with her at the talent show. Meanwhile, Kelsi writes a ballad for Troy and Gabriella. Troy agrees to sing with his friends in the show (&quot;You Are The Music In Me&quot;), not knowing that Sharpay is vying for his attention. (In the extended version, Sharpay and Ryan trap Troy as he prepares for a date with Gabriella, and perform their potential show-stopper (&quot;Humuhumunukunukuapua&#39;a&quot;).)</P>\n<P>Ryan realizes he does not mean much to Sharpay anymore, as she is ready to blow her brother aside for the opportunity to perform with Troy. This leads to tension between the twin siblings and Ryan angrily informs Sharpay that he will no longer obey her orders. Taylor and Gabriella invite Ryan to the baseball game, where he persuades the Wildcats to take part in the talent show (&quot;I Don&#39;t Dance&quot;).</P>\n<P>Troy and Gabriella&#39;s relationship is strained when Troy sees Ryan with Gabriella, sparking jealousy. Owing to a &quot;promise&quot; from Troy, he and Sharpay practice their song for the Midsummer Night&#39;s Talent Show (&quot;You Are The Music In Me (Sharpay Version)&quot;).</P>\n<P>When Sharpay discovers that Ryan and the Wildcats are putting together their own performance in the show, she orders Mr. Fulton to ban all junior staff members from performing. Gabriella angrily confronts Sharpay about her interference and quits her job at Lava Springs. Troy overhears the exchange and tries to persuade Gabriella to change her mind. Gabriella expresses her loss of trust with Troy (&quot;Gotta Go My Own Way&quot;) and leaves Lava Springs, and gives him the necklace back. It also seems that they broke up.</P>\n<P>Troy returns to work the next day to find that his friends refuse to talk to him. Kelsi silently shows Troy the notice from Mr. Fulton, causing Troy to question his own motivations (&quot;Bet On It&quot;). He begins to reconcile with Chad and his other friends. Then Troy confronts Sharpay, informing her that he will not sing with her. The Wildcats and Chad forgive Troy for his absence and convince him to sing in the talent show, which he does only under the condition that they are all allowed to perform as well.</P>\n<P>At Sharpay&#39;s supposed instruction, Ryan gives Troy a new song to learn moments before the show. As Troy goes onstage, he asks Sharpay why she switched the song, and Sharpay is shocked to find that her brother tricked her. Troy sings the song (&quot;Everyday&quot;) alone until Gabriella surprisingly joins him onstage. In the end, Sharpay proudly presents her brother, Ryan, with the award for the talent show. After the talent show, all the Wildcats go to the golf course to enjoy the fireworks.</P>\n<P>Everyone celebrates the end of the summer with a pool party (&quot;All for One&quot;) which features a cameo appearance by <A href="/wiki/Miley_Cyrus" title="Miley Cyrus">Miley Cyrus</A>.</P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Cast">Cast</SPAN></H2>\n<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <A href="/wiki/List_of_High_School_Musical_characters" title="List of High School Musical characters">List of High School Musical characters</A></DIV>\n<UL>\n<LI>Troy Bolton (<A href="/wiki/Zac_Efron" title="Zac Efron">Zac Efron</A>) is Gabriella&#39;s boyfriend, the most popular male student at <I>East High School</I> and the captain of the <A href="/wiki/Varsity_team" title="Varsity team">varsity</A> <A href="/wiki/Basketball" title="Basketball">basketball</A> team. For this movie, Efron did all of his own singing, whereas, in the first <I>High School Musical</I>, his singing was blended with singer <A href="/wiki/Drew_Seeley" title="Drew Seeley">Drew Seeley</A>&#39;s voice.<SUP class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<I><A href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><SPAN title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (October 2012)">citation needed</SPAN></A></I>]</SUP></LI>\n<LI>Gabriella Montez (<A href="/wiki/Vanessa_Hudgens" title="Vanessa Hudgens">Vanessa Hudgens</A>) is Troy&#39;s girlfriend who is relieved that she will still be attending East High. She is the lifeguard at the Lava Springs Country Club until Sharpay&#39;s actions cause her to quit and break up with Troy.</LI>\n<LI>Ryan Evans (<A href="/wiki/Lucas_Grabeel" title="Lucas Grabeel">Lucas Grabeel</A>) is Sharpay&#39;s <A href="/wiki/Twin" title="Twin">twin</A> brother who lives in the shadow of his <A href="/wiki/Primadonna" class="mw-redirect" title="Primadonna">primadonna</A> sister.</LI>\n<LI>Sharpay Evans (<A href="/wiki/Ashley_Tisdale" title="Ashley Tisdale">Ashley Tisdale</A>) is Ryan&#39;s primadonna twin sister determined to win the talent show while also vying for Troy&#39;s attention and doing anything to help him.</LI>\n<LI>Chad Danforth (<A href="/wiki/Corbin_Bleu" title="Corbin Bleu">Corbin Bleu</A>) is Troy&#39;s best friend and is very good friends with Jason and Zeke.</LI>\n<LI>Taylor McKessie (<A href="/wiki/Monique_Coleman" title="Monique Coleman">Monique Coleman</A>) is Gabriella&#39;s best friend. She is also friends with Kelsi Nielsen and Martha Cox and is dating Chad. She is captain of the school Scholastic Decathlon team. She has a summer job at <I>Lava Springs</I> as an Activities Coordinator.</LI>\n<LI>Thomas Fulton (Mark L. Taylor) is the manager of Lava Springs.</LI>\n<LI>Coach Jack Bolton (<A href="/wiki/Bart_Johnson" title="Bart Johnson">Bart Johnson</A>) is Troy&#39;s father and East High&#39;s basketball coach.</LI>\n<LI>Darby Evans (<A href="/wiki/Jessica_Tuck" title="Jessica Tuck">Jessica Tuck</A>) is Sharpay and Ryan&#39;s mother and president of the Lava Springs Board.</LI>\n<LI>Vance Evans (<A href="/wiki/Robert_Curtis_Brown" title="Robert Curtis Brown">Robert Curtis Brown</A>) is Sharpay and Ryan&#39;s father.</LI>\n<LI>Ms. Darbus (<A href="/wiki/Alyson_Reed" title="Alyson Reed">Alyson Reed</A>) is the stern drama teacher at East High.</LI>\n<LI>Zeke Baylor (<A href="/wiki/Chris_Warren_Jr." title="Chris Warren Jr.">Chris Warren Jr.</A>) is friends with Troy and Chad and plays for the basketball team.</LI>\n<LI>Jason Cross (<A href="/wiki/Ryne_Sanborn" title="Ryne Sanborn">Ryne Sanborn</A>) is friends with Troy, Chad, and Zeke and plays on the basketball team.</LI>\n<LI>Kelsi Nielsen (<A href="/wiki/Olesya_Rulin" title="Olesya Rulin">Olesya Rulin</A>) is friends with Gabriella and Taylor and a <A href="/wiki/Pianist" title="Pianist">pianist</A> and <A href="/wiki/Composer" title="Composer">composer</A>.</LI>\n<LI>Martha Cox (<A href="/wiki/Kaycee_Stroh" title="Kaycee Stroh">Kaycee Stroh</A>) is friends with Gabriella, Kelsi, and Taylor.</LI>\n<LI>Jackie (<A href="/wiki/Tanya_Chisholm" title="Tanya Chisholm">Tanya Chisholm</A>) is one of Sharpay’s friends (a.k.a. The Sharpettes).</LI>\n<LI>Lucille Bolton (<A href="/wiki/Leslie_Wing" title="Leslie Wing">Leslie Wing Pomeroy</A>) is Troy&#39;s mother.</LI>\n<LI>Lea (Kelli Baker) is another Sharpette.</LI>\n<LI>Emma (McCall Clark) is another Sharpette.</LI>\n<LI>Unknown Wildcats player (<A href="/wiki/Shane_Harper" title="Shane Harper">Shane Harper</A>) is the principal dancer.</LI>\n<LI>Girl At Pool (<A href="/wiki/Miley_Cyrus" title="Miley Cyrus">Miley Cyrus</A>) is an unknown dancer at the end (cameo).</LI>\n</UL>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Release">Release</SPAN></H2>\n<P>The premiere of <I>High School Musical 2</I> aired at 8 PM <A href="/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone_(North_America)" class="mw-redirect" title="Eastern Time Zone (North America)">Eastern Time</A> on August 17, 2007, and included a telecast hosted by <A href="/wiki/Kenny_Ortega" title="Kenny Ortega">Kenny Ortega</A> and the movie&#39;s cast. On Saturday, August 18, <A href="/wiki/Disney_Channel" title="Disney Channel">Disney Channel</A> aired &quot;High School Musical 2: Wildcat Chat&quot;, in which the stars of the movie answered questions posed by fans. On August 19, Disney aired a sing-along version of the movie.<SUP id="cite_ref-6" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-6">[6]</A></SUP> On May 23, <A href="/wiki/DirecTV" title="DirecTV">DirecTV</A> announced that they would be hosting an exclusive <A href="/wiki/High-definition_video" title="High-definition video">high-definition</A> airing of the movie a few days after the August 17 premiere on its network-only channel, <A href="/wiki/The_101_Network" class="mw-redirect" title="The 101 Network">The 101</A>.<SUP id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-7">[7]</A></SUP></P>\n<P><A href="/wiki/Disney_Channel" title="Disney Channel">Disney Channel</A> aired a weekly program called <I>Road to High School Musical 2</I>, beginning on June 8, 2007, and leading up to the premiere of <I>High School Musical 2</I> in August. The show offered viewers a behind-the-scenes look into the production of the movie. The world premiere of the opening number &quot;<A href="/wiki/What_Time_Is_It%3F_(song)" title="What Time Is It? (song)">What Time Is It</A>&quot; was on <A href="/wiki/Radio_Disney" title="Radio Disney">Radio Disney</A> May 25, 2007,<SUP id="cite_ref-8" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-8">[8]</A></SUP> and similarly &quot;You Are The Music In Me&quot; premiered on July 13, 2007.<SUP id="cite_ref-9" class="reference"><A href="#cite_note-9">[9]</A></SUP></P>\n<P>On December 11, 2007, the movie was released on DVD and Blu-ray titled <I>High School Musical 2: Extended Edition</I>. On September 15, 2008, a 2-disc special edition of the movie was released titled <I>High School Musical 2: Deluxe Dance Edition</I>.</P>\n<H2><SPAN class="mw-headline" id="Songs">Songs</SPAN></H2>\n<DIV role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <A href="/wiki/High_School_Musical_2_(soundtrack)" title="High School Musical 2 (soundtrack)">High School Musical 2 (soundtrack)</A></DIV>\n<TABLE class="wikitable">\n<TBODY><TR>\n<TH>Song</TH>\n<TH>Chiefly sung by</TH>\n<TH>Other singers</TH>\n<TH>Scene</TH>\n</TR>\n<TR>\n<TD><I><B><A href="/wiki/What_Time_Is_It%3F_(song)" title="What Time Is It?
